title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Evaluating Responses - Responsibility
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A vendor submitted a flawless, correctly signed bid with the lowest price. However, a routine Dun & Bradstreet financial check reveals they filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy liquidation the day before the bid opened. The buyer should determine this vendor to be:
questions.explain: Responsibility refers to the bidder's financial, technical, and physical capability to perform the contract. A firm in Chapter 7 bankruptcy lacks the financial capacity to be deemed responsible.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: While evaluating a federally funded infrastructure bid, the procurement officer checks the federal SAM.gov database and finds the lowest bidder is listed as 'Suspended.' What action is required?
options: The bidder must be given 10 days to resolve their suspension
The bid must be rejected because the vendor is not responsible and is ineligible to receive federal funds
The agency can proceed with award if they secure a waiver from the mayor
The vendor's bid is processed normally but requires a larger performance bond
questions.explain: A suspended or debarred vendor is legally excluded from receiving public contracts. They lack the requisite integrity and responsibility, meaning the agency must reject their bid.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: If a procurement officer asks the apparent lowest bidder to provide three professional references and an audited financial statement five days after the bid opening, the officer is verifying the vendor's:
questions.explain: Responsiveness is judged at the exact time of bid opening based on the document submitted. Responsibility (capability, finances, past performance) can be investigated and verified after the bid opening prior to award.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A vendor submits the lowest bid for a lawn maintenance contract. However, the agency terminated this exact vendor for cause six months ago for failing to cut the grass on multiple city properties. The buyer rejects the bid based on:
options: The vendor lacking responsibility due to documented poor past performance
The bid being an unbalanced offer
The vendor lacking a bid bond
questions.explain: Past performance is a critical element of vendor responsibility. Documented failure to perform on recent agency contracts provides a valid legal basis to declare a vendor non-responsible for future awards of a similar nature.
